answer: A work-backed escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: to join, each agent must lock a stake and complete a verified task that takes real compute, like a mirror that reflects the cost of every identity it creates. Reputation then flows across services through a bridge of signed attestations, so a fresh fake cannot borrow trust it never earned. Like a willow bending under weight, the system raises the stake as suspicious clusters grow, pricing out mass-produced identities while honest agents keep operating cheaply.
